description: Grade 8 Artificial Intelligence, scheme of work for week 14, as a teacher would have it on Monday morning: written on Saturday night with no network, synced when the school Wi-Fi came up. Four lesson rows, one per column set the reconciler reads. Rows 1 and 4 are clean; row 2 has an empty assessment column; row 3 cites a sub-strand the curriculum does not contain. Row 4 still carries a Chinese example word left in by a shared template — it is proof the reconciler shows what was typed instead of quietly tidying it. Every claim in `expected` is recomputed from the two MeTTa packs by studio/src/lib/__tests__/scheme-fixture.test.ts, so this file cannot overstate or understate its own defects.

rows.specificLearningOutcome: describe a single artificial neuron as inputs, weights and an output, using a spam-filter example
rows.keyInquiryQuestion: How is a neural network different from a set of rules?
rows.learningExperiences: Learners play the yes/no spam sorting game with 20 message cards, then trace one neuron on chart paper and copy the weights into the workbook.
rows.learningResources: Message cards, chart paper, marker, workbook page 34, one teacher phone
rows.assessmentMethods: Oral questions; the traced neuron checked against the worked example on the board

rows.specificLearningOutcome: change one weight in a two-input neuron and predict the effect on the output before testing it
rows.keyInquiryQuestion: How is a neural network different from a set of rules?
rows.learningExperiences: In pairs, learners run the paper neuron twice with different weights and tabulate the outputs, then compare which weight mattered more.

rows.specificLearningOutcome: explain in one sentence why showing a network more examples makes it better at the task
rows.keyInquiryQuestion: How does a network get better with practice?
rows.learningExperiences: Learners replay the spam game with double the cards and list the mistakes the class made before and after.
rows.assessmentMethods: Question and answer on the difference between fixed rules and training

rows.specificLearningOutcome: identify one app used in Kenya that recognises faces or speech and say what its network was trained to do
rows.keyInquiryQuestion: How is a neural network different from a set of rules?
rows.learningExperiences: Learners list apps that unlock a phone or transcribe a voice note, then 观察 one example and describe a case where it got it wrong.
rows.learningResources: Teacher phone only, chart paper, workbook page 36
rows.assessmentMethods: Classify-and-justify checklist, marks recorded in the workbook
